entries.english:
83. King Friedrich's safe-conduct for the Bohemian deputies. August 1448. Register no. 2472.

Friedrich, etc. Let it be known, etc. The most reverend father in Christ, our dearest friend Herr Johannes, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church of Sant'Angelo and legate a latere of the Apostolic See, has arranged a general diet at our city of Vienna on the feast of St. Giles, to be attended by our majesty and the illustrious and noble barons, knights and squires, and the honorable and distinguished community of Prague and other communities of the renowned kingdom of Bohemia, for mutual negotiations concerning the welfare of that kingdom and the peaceful state of our principalities and dominions.

Wishing to ensure the safety of the barons, noble landholders and envoys and representatives of Prague and the other cities and communities who will come on behalf of that kingdom, so that they may come, stay and return with all their retinues free from every danger, we freely grant our royal safe-conduct, firmly valid until the next feast of St. Gall, and full security to be observed inviolably. It is granted to Ulrich and Heinrich de Rosenberg; Meinhard de Nova domo; Alssoni de Sternberg; Georg de Kunstat et de Podiebrad; Nicolaus and Sbynko Lepus de Hasenburg; Hynko Crussina de Stvanberg; Hans de Rysenberg et de Rabie; Hassko de Waldenstein; Wenzel de Michelspcrg; Hans de Novadomo; Sdenko de Sternberg; Hans and Heinrich de Colowrath; Hans and Heinrich de Strasz; Heinrich de Michalowitz; Hans Burian de Gutenstein; Alssoni de Zeberg; Wilhelm de Eylburg; Hans de Smirzitz; Nicolaus de Lypa; Przibiko de Clenowi; Hans de Sutitz; Bohus and Sdenko de Postupitz; Jakob de Wrzessowitz; Dietrich de Myletinka; Nicolaus and Hans de Lobkowitz; Hans de Militzin; and the honorable and prudent representatives of Prague and the other towns, and all other deputies and non-deputies accompanying them, whom we wish to be treated as named individually, whether ecclesiastical or secular and whatever their status, condition or dignity. It covers all their subjects and household members in their company, jointly and separately, up to one thousand horses and the same number of persons, or fewer as they wish.

We assure them by these presents that, within those limits and during that period, they may freely travel through all our lands and jurisdictions to Vienna for the diet, remain, speak and negotiate with us, and finally, whether negotiations are concluded or not, return peacefully and quietly to their homes or go to other places of their choice, with their persons and all their goods safe and without hindrance or injury. We promise on our royal word to observe the safe-conduct sincerely, completely and inviolably, without deceit, for ourselves and all princes, counts, nobles, knights, citizens of Vienna and other towns and those attached or allied to our majesty.

For greater security, if anyone in their company causes damage, obstruction or insulting words to our servants or subjects, or conversely our household or subjects do so to theirs, which God forbid, the safe-conduct shall not thereby be considered violated; instead, the parties shall make due redress for the wrong. We therefore firmly and strictly command all subjects of our principalities and lands, whatever their status or condition, to allow the said barons, nobles, townsmen and representatives of the kingdom and all their companions to enjoy this security peacefully and without hindrance on their journey to Vienna, during their stay and on their return, and to show them every honor and favor, presuming to do nothing otherwise.
